Meridian Central Station.basicInfo: The big Victorian terminus of Kestrel Bay, still busy until the last Line 9 train leaves at 23:45. After that the concourse shutters and the platforms go quiet until the first train at 05:30.
Meridian Central Station.hiddenInfo: The signal box shorted at 23:31 because a frightened teenager hiding in the maintenance tunnel panicked; his power kills electronics. The service door at the end of Platform 4 is not locked tonight.

platform-4.description: The last-train platform: yellow edge line, a wall clock that runs a minute slow, a bench with a broken slat and a fluorescent tube that will not stop flickering. A steel service door stands at the far end, painted the same grey as the wall.

concourse.description: The main hall after dark: shuttered kiosks, a departure board stuck on one line, and a busker's corner by the closed coffee stand where a theremin hums to the empty tiles.

signal-box.description: A locked brick cabin at the platform throat with a keypad door and a window of old wired glass. Its relays shorted at 23:31 and the whole line is held until someone can sign it safe.

maintenance-tunnel.description: Behind the service door at the end of Platform 4: a low, dark, dripping tunnel with a handrail, cable trays overhead and a chalked warning on the wall. Torches and phones behave badly here.

Line 9 Night Train.basicInfo: The last Line 9 service, four carriages of worn blue seats, running from Meridian Central to the end of the line at Harrow Street. It is held at Platform 4 until the signal box is signed safe.
Line 9 Night Train.hiddenInfo: Tib planned to ride the rear carriage so he could keep an eye on the tunnel mouth and the case. The driver knows nothing and wants the incident paperwork over.

rear-carriage.description: The last carriage: a dozen empty seats, a map of Line 9 with the stops pinned in black, a cracked window and a rack where a bag or a case can be tucked out of the way.

drivers-cab.description: A narrow cab with a dim dashboard, a thermos on the shelf and a radio that crackles with line control. The driver is a patient man who wants the paperwork finished.

Harrow Street Depot.basicInfo: The end of Line 9: a rail yard with a loading bay, a small night office and a gate that stays open until dawn. It is where Tib's errand ends.
Harrow Street Depot.hiddenInfo: The drop point on the case's label is the loading bay. The Achterberg family home is a short walk from the depot, and that is where Tib means to take his brother tonight.

loading-bay.description: A concrete bay under sodium lamps with roller doors, pallets of parcels and a courier's cage. This is the drop point on the case's label.

night-office.description: A warm little office with a kettle, a timetable wall and a desk lamp. A logbook records who comes in after midnight, and the door has a window onto the yard.
